question: Does the published genome-wide elastic-net dependency predictor of Shi et al. (2024) reproduce on the project's 773-identity development cohort, and how does it compare with the saved wide300 and panel30 ridge references on identical folds?
intended_decision: Whether the published elastic net should replace or join wide300 as the project's development reference, and how to read the published method's reported predictability; benchmark scores are surrogate evidence for experimental prioritization.
hypothesis: H1: the genome-wide elastic net, fitted fold-locally, matches or exceeds wide300 on development mean Spearman. Falsifier: adapted minus wide300 below zero with the paired identity bootstrap interval excluding zero. H2: the in-sample correlation computed by the authors' public script overstates out-of-fold correlation on this cohort. Falsifier: mean exact-arm resubstitution Pearson minus adapted OOF Pearson at or below 0.02.
data_and_cohort: DepMap 24Q2 OmicsExpressionProteinCodingGenesTPMLogp1.csv (sha256 39eff342..., data/source-lock.json, CC BY 4.0) restricted to the 18,953 genes of the saved wide300 universe; outcomes and identities from research/readiness-20261021/development.csv (773 identities, one per group). No Broad, historical-final or Sanger outcomes.
targets: All 12 inherited targets, declared before scoring: BRAF, KRAS, NRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, PIK3CA, SMARCA2, SMARCA4, ARID1B, STAG1, MDM2, PRMT5.
baseline: Saved wide300 and panel30 ridge OOF predictions and the lineage baseline in research/wide-expression-20261021/models.json; positive control replays saved MDM2 wide300/panel30 OOF from this extraction (max abs difference 1.4e-14 and 1.3e-15).
metrics: Primary: 12-target mean development OOF Spearman difference, elastic net minus wide300. Secondary: minus panel30 and lineage, per-target Spearman, MSE and Pearson, nonzero coefficient counts, lambda boundary hits, resubstitution versus OOF Pearson, R > 0.2 pass counts. Coverage: all 773 rows for every target.
search_space: One method: elastic net with l1_ratio 0.5 on the glmnet default 100-lambda path; no other mixing values, feature screens or model families. Stage 1 is an oracle-lambda ceiling over the same path and is not a candidate.
budget: About 30 min price, 70 min adapted, 60 min exact wall time on 2 CPU workers under a 12 GiB cap; one new download (the pinned 461 MB 24Q2 expression matrix, hash-verified, not committed).
exposure_status: Development outcomes were used by the earlier wide300 trial and are not fresh; Broad already exposed and not used here; historical final not fresh and not used; Sanger reserved and not opened.
evaluation_plan: Saved outer folds (5, seed 1701, identity-grouped); imputation, z-scoring and lambda selection inside every training fold with 3 inner folds (seed 817). Stage 1 ceiling computed and inspected before stage 2; stages 2 and 3 run regardless of stage 1. Grouped random folds do not establish transfer.
success_and_failure: Success is a reproducible, fold-matched published reference with all 12 targets and all failures retained, plus a quantified reading of the published metric. A negative comparison with wide300 is a reported result, not a failure to hide. Any target-wise favorable subset is post hoc.
outside_review: Independent computational replay, assay-aware scientific review, and a check of the published-method mapping (glmnet versus sklearn, missing Celligner alignment) remain necessary before acceptance.
